thread_analysis.thread_summary: This internal thread (February 18-20, 2025) tracks review of an RF test report for ALPS Alpine (project [ID], Test Result: PASS). Sakai first corrects inconsistent packet-type abbreviations in the report to match the log files. A second reviewer, Tanaka, then flags that the TRM/CA/[ID] test item was tested at both Max Power and Min Power but the report table only showed the Max Power row, requesting a Min Power row be added. Sakai confirms the root cause: when ICS 1/4 Power Control is YES, TRM/CA requires an additional Min Power measurement, which was missed because the report was created by overwriting a past template without re-checking this ICS setting. Sakai issues a corrected report and instructs the team to check ICS 1/4 Power Control:YES/NO whenever reusing a past RF report as a template. Tanaka confirms the corrected report has no issues, and Ushiroebisu places the final report and PDF on the project server.
all_questions_found: (Internal) Is this RF test report for ALPS Alpine complete and correct, including consistent packet-type naming matching the log files?
(Internal) Should the TRM/CA/[ID] test item's report table include a Min Power row in addition to the Max Power row, given it was tested at both?
(Internal, implicit) What should be checked going forward when an RF report is created by overwriting a past report as a template?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Packet-type abbreviations in the RF report table (DH1, 2-DH1, 3-DH1, DH3, DH5, 2-DH5, 3-DH5) were corrected to match the underlying log files for consistency. The TRM/CA/[ID] test item was tested at both Max Power and Min Power, but the report table initially only contained the Max Power row. Sakai explained that when the device's ICS answer for '1/4 Power Control' is YES, TRM/CA requires an additional Min Power measurement row in the report. This was missed in the initial report because it was prepared by overwriting a past report template without re-checking the ICS 1/4 Power Control setting for this project.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Report review proceeded in stages: an initial formatting/consistency correction (packet abbreviations), followed by a substantive completeness check (Min Power row for TRM/CA) by a second reviewer. The root cause (ICS 1/4 Power Control:YES requiring an additional Min Power test row) was identified and the corrected report issued before final sign-off. A process improvement was proposed: always re-verify the ICS 1/4 Power Control setting when reusing a past report as a template.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: An RF test report missing the Min Power row required when ICS 1/4 Power Control is YES is incomplete and must be corrected after review, causing rework and potential delay. Reusing past report templates without re-checking project-specific ICS answers can systematically propagate this kind of omission across projects.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: The initial RF test report omitted the Min Power test row for TRM/CA/[ID] despite the device's ICS 1/4 Power Control being YES (which requires it), because the report was created by overwriting a past template without re-checking this ICS setting - an error the reviewer (Sakai) acknowledged as his own oversight ('I also missed this in my check').
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When preparing or reviewing an RF test report, always check the device's ICS 1/4 Power Control answer: if YES, TRM/CA must include both Max Power and Min Power rows. When reusing a past RF report as a template, explicitly re-verify this ICS setting for the new project rather than assuming it carries over, and ensure packet-type naming in the report matches the underlying log files.
